item.title: Where Is the Friend's House?
item.description: A group of boys are having fun and playing during class. Their teacher is a few minutes late, and they take full advantage of this, disrupting other classes and joking around. Once their teacher finally comes in, he scolds them profusely and tells them that they should study next time. He comes around collecting homework and stops at Mohammad Reza Nematzadeh’s desk. Mohammad fumbles for his homework, but the teacher is most displeased when he realizes that Mohammad did his homework on loose sheets of paper instead of his notebook. The teacher chides Mohammad, saying that if he did this one more time, he would be expelled. Mohammad cries and promises to always use his notebook for homework. His friend, Ahmad, sits beside him, trying to comfort him.

item.title: Strange Case of 0.9999.....
item.description:
My friends and I sat on the lawn, discussing what we were going to do at our next sleepover. We planned out the perfect schedule. We would eat dinner, pizza of course, then we would set up our sleeping bags. We would watch movies, play for some time,……. but then what? We didn’t have any idea on what to do during that time.

One of my friends suggested playing truth or dare, but the idea was shot down, since we have already played it too many times. My other friend suggested playing skeletons in the closet, but we had already shared all of our secrets, we had nothing else. Then, I suggested just sharing cool facts that we know. My friends all agreed, and we decided to have a trial run, to have a better idea on how it would go during the sleepover.

item.title: Osama - A Girl Without a Name
item.description: You’re shoved into a two by two room by the royal guards. Their faces are emotionless as they silently lock the door and close the ceiling. This is the punishment for your crime. Sitting is impossible - so you stand, ignoring the ache in your feet. This is your death sentence. You take a while to look around, observe your surroundings. You realize there are holes for oxygen to come through, but where is the slot for food and water? You decide to just wait for a few minutes. But those minutes turn into hours, and soon it is nighttime. That’s when it dawns on you, no one is coming to give you food and water. You tell yourself you’ll survive, but you know that isn’t true. Soon, days turn into weeks and by then, you’re dying of thirst and starvation. Hunger rips apart your insides and your throat is so dry you cannot even scream. Soon you collapse and die. This was a real punishment in the period of Kings. People would die of thirst and starvation over the course of a few weeks. Now imagine, the small room is an entire country. Instead of one prisoner, there are millions of women waiting for a slow death. That is the story of Osama.

item.title: Three Women, One Dream: Freedom
item.description:
What does freedom mean?

Does it mean being allowed to play outside? Being allowed to ride a bicycle? Being allowed to spend your own money? The Day I Became a Woman explores these questions through three stories about women at different ages…….

It is a windy day and Hava’s mom is waking Hava up from her bed inside of a small white - cloth tent. Hava is a small, energetic girl with black, wavy hair up to her shoulders with short bangs. She is wearing sandals and a frock that hangs up to her knees. She lives with her grandmother and mother. They are a Muslim family living in Iran, and in her tradition, a girl becomes a woman on her ninth birthday. Once Hava gets out of bed, she is informed by her grandmother that it is her birthday. Therefore, Hava has now become a woman. She must wear a Chador and she cannot talk or play with boys. Hava’s grandmother and mother immediately start sewing Hava a Chador to wear.

item.title: Who Actually Makes Rainbows?
item.description: My little brother invited his friend over for a playdate at our house. They ate snacks, played, and ended up watching a TV show called “My Little Pony”. It is a kids show featuring unicorns. I glanced over at the TV screen and watched a scene about a young unicorn sliding on the rainbow. The rainbow was solid, and included the color pink!(Since it is a kids show, I let it slide…) According to the character on the TV show, rainbows are made by pegasus ponies in a factory on Cloudsdale. Now, this made me wonder, how are rainbows actually made? Are they really made by pegasus ponies in a factory on Cloudsdale? These are the questions I will be answering today. Let’s go!

item.title: How to Measure a Building Without Touching It
item.description: I have this big hole on my face called my mouth… and I probably should have kept it shut. One day, I peeked ahead in my math book and saw a chapter on trigonometry. Out of curiosity, I asked my dad what it meant… and that’s when things got interesting. My dad explained the basics and asked me a question. How would you try and find the height of the building?

item.title: The Geometry of Survival: The Triangle Rescue Mission
item.description: Yesterday, I invited my friend over to my house for a play date. My friend is smart and always has good ideas on what to do. We played for hours and eventually got bored. So, she started looking through my math worksheets on geometry. Then, she asked me “What is the point of knowing all these concepts? Where are you going to use this in the real world?”. Testing time…..!!!

item.title: When Lines Just Touch: The Secret of Tangents
item.description:
I was watching the movie Aladdin when my dad walked in and said “Let’s do something tangential to watching the movie!”. I asked, “what is a tangent?”. After a short session on tangents I ended up with this problem.

Here is the problem:

AB = 9, BC = 12, and triangle ABC is a right-angled triangle. The two circles have the same area. Find the combined area of the 2 circles.

item.title: A radical's take on radicals: Square Root without using a calculator
item.description:
You walk into class and realize today is the day of your square roots test. You sit down and grab your calculator. You put in the question and the calculator gives you the answer. Seems simple, right? But for over two thousand years, how did people find square roots? It wasn’t as simple as just asking AI. Luckily, an abundance of different ways were discovered. Some of them are:

1. Babylonian/Heron's method
2. Approximation method
3. Bakhshali's method

and many more.Today, I want to share what I learned about the Babylonian method.

item.title: Cracking the Code: How Secrets Traveled During World War II
item.description: The cryptanalysts stayed up all night long, waiting for a message to be given. They had grown paranoid since they hadn’t gotten any new messages for the past two weeks. Until one of them picked up a message through her headphones, she positioned her fingers on the enigma machine ready to translate the message. She translated it and the resulting message was in German. It read “Bitte…Bitte…”, it meant “Please…Please” in English. She was alarmed and she listened for another part of the message, but it had gone silent. This is an example of an alarming situation that the cryptanalysts had to go through during World War two. One very outstanding cryptanalyst was Joan Clarke. She worked at Bletchley Park, a secret codebreaking center in England, in Hut 8. The reason why she was outstanding was because, despite being a female in a male - dominated field, she gained their trust and respect. Because of this, today I am going to show you many different ways of communication during the war, and how to use them. Let’s start!

item.title: A4 Paper Has a Superpower… and It’s Pure Math
item.description:
Math is everywhere, even in places you will not expect it to be in. It might even be in the sheet of paper that you use everyday…

Have you ever looked down at your desk and tried to find out the dimensions of your paper? Most people do not, but I can change your mind about that. Let us start with the size of A4 paper. The dimensions of A4 paper are 210 mm x 297 mm. But, why? Why is it that A4 paper has to be of those dimensions? Why not 225 mm x 325 mm. Or 765 mm x 150 mm. That is what I am going to explain, along with many other things today. Let’s start!

item.title: Shakuntala Devi - A week of Puzzles
item.description:
“Math — it’s a puzzle. I love figuring out puzzles.” — said Maya Lin.

There have been many brilliant women who made history in mathematics, and Shakuntala Devi was one of them. She was a mathematician and writer who amazed the world with her mental calculations. She once solved the 23rd root of a 201-digit number in just 50 seconds, and even multiplied two 13-digit numbers faster than a computer!

item.title: Ratios, Tables, and One Very Proud 90’s Kid
item.description: “This method never failed me in 25 years!!!”, declared my dad. He is a 90’s kid. You know, the kids who had a secret crush on their teachers(yikes), who played with Tamagotchi(seriously?), who thought the world was simple and beautiful(spoiler alert: it wasn’t!) back then, and their old - school method of studying is better(not always).But, I have to agree there are instances where some of their methods are easy to understand and surprisingly useful.

item.title: Five Fun Ways to Multiply (Without a Calculator!)
item.description:
Today, I had an interesting conversation with my friends. It was about different types of multiplication. Surprisingly, they knew only one method of multiplication and in one case did not understand the underlying meaning of multiplication. So, I explained to them the five methods that I knew.I thought it would be great to share this knowledge with others.

Method 1:Repetitive Addition

The first method is called “repetitive addition”. In fact,this explains the underlying meaning of multiplication. In this method we simply write out our multiplication equation in terms of addition.
